items.headline: Overnight pulse (10pm CT): DXY 102.04, EUR/USD 1.1174 (-0.39% day), GBP/USD 1.3341 (-0.28%), USD/JPY 157.69 (+0.55%), gold $4,019.80 (-0.46%), WTI $100.80 (-0.94%), US 10Y 4.99% — dollar marginally firmer into Tuesday Asia ahead of the central-bank week

Reuters Tuesday Asia: yen slips to 157.73 (-0.16%), eroding last week's haven gains on risk-on mood and a weaker euro ahead of the Fed/BoE/ECB/BoJ week; BoJ seen holding at 1.25% Friday with December hike odds slightly better than even; services PPI 3.7% inline

Dallas Fed manufacturing Oct 13.4 (vs 7.0 fcst, Sep 9.8) — headline beat, internals split: new orders 9.3 (vs 30.7 Sep), production 15.8, prices paid 55.3, future index 38.1; dollar firmed into the NY close on the oil/geopolitics bid rather than the survey alone

NY close: see markets.json — levels at the 3:00 PM CT close; dollar firmed on the day (DXY ~102.00) as oil eased (Brent settled $115.81, -0.8%; WTI $101.76, -1.5%) on Qatar-mediated de-escalation hopes while Houthi claims on Saudi pipeline/airport targets continued without Riyadh confirmation

items.headline: CBI Oct: retail sales balance -10 (vs -47 fcst, Sep -55) — slowest fall since Apr 2025; orders -36 (vs -62 Sep); CBI: outlook fragile into Wednesday's Budget; sterling eased anyway ($1.3348)
German Ifo Oct 90.2 (vs 90.0 fcst, Sep 89.9) — sixth straight rise, highest since May 2023; expectations 91.6, current conditions 88.8; Fuest: 'The economic recovery is continuing'
Reuters Monday Asia: currencies in tight ranges into the central-bank week — DXY 101.64, euro $1.122, sterling $1.3385, yen 156.92; 10Y 4.974% as the oil pullback eases the dollar
Qatari mediators in Tehran Sunday in a US-coordinated de-escalation effort (Reuters); Brent bounced off Asia lows to $115.48, WTI $102.08 — war premium easing, not gone

Oil slides to fresh Asia lows as Brent breaks below $115 — $114.60 (-1.8%), WTI $101.13 (-2.1%) at the 0232 GMT print; Houthi attacks on Saudi targets continue, Saudi intercepts reported, no announced damage

Houthis renew warning against using Riyadh's King Khalid airport — Saree: airport remains a 'military target', operations targeting it will continue; airport designates Terminal 1 domestic / Terminal 2 international from Sunday (Reuters, Oct 24)
